What I changed in Change Stack

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

I wanted to keep the file, explanation, and review progress connected. I kept file-by-file review and changed how you move between those things.

What got in the wayWhat I changed
The layer, file path, and file position are spread across the screen.I kept the layer, file, and path together. Previous and Next switch files directly; the position opens the searchable nine-file list. Each file keeps its reading position.
Several rows of file controls compete with the diff.I put frequent file actions in one toolbar and kept Submit review in the PR header. Focus condenses the heading and hides both side panels without losing your place.
The 37-summary count belongs to the layer. access.ts has six.I labeled both counts and kept the summary-to-code link. Matching highlights preserve green addition text. The full captured summary expands without losing its place when marked seen.
Seen summaries, viewed files, and a submitted review mean different things.PR progress and the seven included demo files have separate counts. Opening a file never marks it viewed. Summary seen and the final decision stay separate. Viewed changes can be undone.

The right panel takes space

Context takes code width. Z hides it; below 1280px it becomes an overlay. Split has continuous panes and optional line wrapping. Local notes have their own index, separate from source comments.

What I checked

The comparison keeps all seven imports, the full source summary, and captured layer progress. I checked file switching, linked ranges, draft recovery, Undo, keyboard access, and dialog focus. I haven’t measured a speed improvement or tested this with developers.

What I’d test next

I kept M because each explanation can be checked against the diff. Other approaches change the reading order. In Paper, I sketched tighter statement anchors, paired-file inspection, and a private question queue, each with a test and tradeoff.

This uses the out-of-date Formbricks #8650 snapshot at 23cdac2. Seven of 52 diffs are included. Other content is labeled as a preview; not every source workflow is implemented. Submitting a review is simulated and sends nothing.
